Switch Games Digital vs Physical: Which Should You Buy in 2026?

Roundup · Updated 2026-08-07

It's the question every new Switch owner hits: download it, or buy the cartridge? Neither is "wrong," but they fit different players. Here's the real trade-off in 2026 — price, resale, storage, and convenience — so you can stop second-guessing the checkout button.

Price: physical usually wins on first-party

Nintendo rarely discounts its own digital games at the eShop outside seasonal sales, while boxed cartridges get undercut by Amazon and other retailers year-round. For a popular first-party title, the physical cart is almost always cheaper than the eShop version on any given day.

Mario Kart 8 Deluxe (physical) Tears of the Kingdom (physical)

Resale & lending: only physical counts

A cartridge can be sold, traded, or lent to a friend when you're done. A digital license is tied to your Nintendo Account forever. If you like recycling your library or handing games to a sibling, physical is the only option that holds value.

Storage: digital eats your SD card

Switch carts are tiny but the games aren't — a big title can be 10–15 GB. Fill the console with downloads and you'll need a microSD card sooner than you'd like, and those aren't free. Physical games run off the cart, leaving your internal storage for saves and a few small downloads.

Convenience: digital is instant

No swapping carts, no "where did I put Mario Kart," and you can buy from the couch at midnight. For households with multiple players on one console, digital means everyone's library is always available. That convenience is worth real money to some buyers.

Collectibility & cartridges

There's a quiet joy to a shelf of Switch carts, and limited editions (especially Zelda) have become collector items. If you like owning things physically, that alone can settle the debate.

Our recommendation by player type

  • Best price + resale: buy physical on Amazon.
  • Multiple players, one console, instant access: buy digital, but wait for an eShop sale.
  • Collecting or lending: physical, every time.
  • Tight on SD storage: physical saves you a microSD purchase.

Where to buy each cheapest

Physical: track Amazon for the lowest mainstream price (see our full where-to-buy comparison). Digital: only the eShop carries Switch downloads, so your lever is timing — buy during Nintendo's seasonal sales or with discounted eShop gift cards.
